assignment.title: The Great Barrier Reef: Ocean Giants & Coral Wonders
assignment.instructions: Listen attentively to the audio track. You have a maximum of 2 listens. When you are ready, answer all 10 Cambridge Stage 6 comprehension questions.

questions.question: What is the primary natural habitat described in the audio?
questions.explanation: The speaker introduces the coral reef marine ecosystem as the central focus.

questions.question: According to the speaker, why are coral reefs often called the 'rainforests of the sea'?
options: Because heavy rain falls on them every day
Because they contain an immense variety of marine biodiversity
Because tall seaweed trees grow out of them
Because freshwater rivers flow directly through them
questions.explanation: Reefs support extraordinary biodiversity, matching the species richness of rainforests.

questions.question: What role do tiny algae (zooxanthellae) play in the survival of coral polyps?
options: They clean the ocean surface from debris
They act as shields against predator sharks
They freeze water to create solid rock
questions.explanation: The algae convert sunlight into essential food energy for the corals.

questions.question: What meaning of the word 'vibrant' best matches its use in the description of the reef fish?
questions.explanation: In Cambridge Stage 6 contexts, 'vibrant' describes brilliant, radiant colours and energetic life.

questions.question: Which creature uses camouflage to blend seamlessly into the sandy seafloor?
questions.explanation: Stingrays and flatfish use coloration to conceal themselves in sand.

questions.question: What warning does the narrator give regarding rising ocean temperatures?
options: Corals may undergo bleaching and lose their vital algae
Reefs will expand uncontrollably toward the shore
Fish will permanently abandon the oceans for rivers
The ocean water will evaporate completely
questions.explanation: Warm waters stress corals, expelling algae and resulting in coral bleaching.

questions.question: What can be inferred about the narrator's tone throughout the presentation?
questions.explanation: The presenter speaks with enthusiasm, scientific care, and conservation respect.

questions.question: In the phrase 'fragile equilibrium', what does 'equilibrium' mean?
questions.explanation: Equilibrium means a delicate, interconnected balance in nature.

questions.question: Which of the following actions was recommended to help preserve coral reefs?
options: Collecting living corals as travel souvenirs
Reducing plastic waste and lowering carbon emissions
Building deeper artificial marinas directly on reefs
questions.explanation: Responsible conservation requires cutting carbon emissions and plastic pollution.

questions.question: What is the overall main purpose of this listening audio?
options: To advertise holiday resorts and diving equipment
To entertain listeners with fictional legends
To educate students on reef ecosystems and advocate for ocean protection
questions.explanation: The core aim is educational awareness and inspiring stewardship of marine habitats.
